$R:D_0(\Omega)\to C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, where
$D_0(\Omega)=\{h\in C_c^\infty(\Omega):\int_\Omega h=0\}$, such that
$\operatorname{div}Rh=h$. For each compact $K\subset\Omega$ there is a compact

on $(0,\infty)\times\Omega$. Its normalization may be fixed by any
$\theta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $\int_\Omega\theta=1$ through
$\langle\pi,a(t)\theta(x)\rangle=0$ for every compactly supported smooth
temporal test $a$. Pressure is unique under this normalization. This is a
conditional distributional statement and gives no $L^2$ pressure estimate,
corner regularity, or pointwise boundary traction. Here

items.actual_scope:
Let $L>0$ be the numerical period in the declared SI metre unit, with physical side length $L\,\mathrm m$; let $\rho_0>0$ be constant in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$ and $\mu>0$ constant in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$. Set $\nu=\mu/\rho_0>0$. On $\mathbb T_L^3$, use normalized Lebesgue measure $L^{-3}dx$, and let $H$ be the real $L^2$ vector fields whose divergence vanishes distributionally, with unrestricted mean mode, and $V=H\cap H^1$, where $H^1$ consists of fields and first weak derivatives in $L^2$. Here $H^s_\sigma$ means the real Fourier-weighted Sobolev space with weights $(1+L^2|\kappa_k|^2)^s$, Fourier divergence condition $k\cdot\widehat u(k)=0$ for $k\ne0$, and unrestricted constant mode. Let $u_0\in H$ be an initial velocity measured in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Assume Countable Choice and the finite-dimensional ODE principle that on any closed cylinder in a finite-dimensional real normed space where a vector field $F$ is bounded by $B$ and is $L_F$-Lipschitz in its state variable, its integral map on continuous curves within radius $r$ of the initial value is invariant if $hB\le r$ and is a contraction if $hL_F<1$, where $h$ is the time-interval length. Then the adopted unforced periodic model has a global weak velocity $u\in C_w([0,\infty);H)\cap L^\infty(0,\infty;H)\cap L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(0,\infty;V)$, where $C_w$ means continuity of each fixed $H$-pairing and the time-dependent spaces are strongly measurable Bochner spaces, with $u(0)=u_0$ and strong $H$ trace at zero. For every smooth real periodic divergence-free test field $\phi$ compactly supported in time it satisfies
$$
\int_0^\infty\!\bigl[(u,\partial_t\phi)+(u\otimes u,\nabla\phi)-\nu(\nabla u,\nabla\phi)\bigr]dt+(u_0,\phi(0))=0,
$$
where the spatial pairings use the normalized measure and $(u\otimes u):\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}u_i u_j\partial_j\phi_i$. It also satisfies, for every $t\ge0$,
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_0^t\|\nabla u(s)\|_2^2ds\le\|u_0\|_2^2,
$$
and there is a full-measure set $S\subset(0,\infty)$ such that for every $s\in S\cup\{0\}$ and every $t\ge s$,
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_s^t\|\nabla u(\tau)\|_2^2d\tau\le\|u(s)\|_2^2.
$$
In SI units the kinetic energy is $K(t)=\frac{\rho_0}{2}\int_{[0,L]^3}|u(t,x)|^2dx$, and the inequality implies
$$
K(t)+\mu\int_0^t\int_{[0,L]^3}|\nabla u(s,x)|^2dx\,ds\le K(0).
$$
There is also a full-measure set $S\subset(0,\infty)$ such that for every $s\in S\cup\{0\}$ and every $t\ge s$,
$$
K(t)+\mu\int_s^t\int_{[0,L]^3}|\nabla u(\tau,x)|^2dx\,d\tau\le K(s).
$$
This is a conditional model deduction about velocity; it asserts no pressure regularity, weak uniqueness, global smoothness, or empirical validity.

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be any nonempty bounded open set in Cartesian coordinates measured in metres. Define $D_\sigma(\Omega)=\{a\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\operatorname{div}a=0\}$, let $H$ be its $L^2(\Omega)$ closure, and let $V$ be its closure in $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, where $H_0^1$ is the $H^1$ closure of compactly supported smooth fields and $H^1$ has the norm formed from the $L^2$ norms of a field and its first weak derivatives. Let $\rho_0>0$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $\mu>0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, $\nu=\mu/\rho_0$, and $u_0\in H$ be an initial velocity in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice, and the finite-dimensional ODE principle that on any closed cylinder in a finite-dimensional real normed space where a vector field $F$ is bounded by $B$ and is $L_F$-Lipschitz in its state variable, its integral map on continuous curves within radius $r$ of the initial value is invariant if $hB\le r$ and is a contraction if $hL_F<1$, where $h$ is the time-interval length. Then the adopted unforced no-slip model has
$$
u\in C_w([0,\infty);H)\cap L^\infty(0,\infty;H)\cap L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(0,\infty;V),
$$
where $C_w$ means continuity of every fixed $H$-pairing and the time-dependent spaces are Bochner spaces of strongly measurable maps, with $u(0)=u_0$, strong $H$ trace at zero, and, for every compactly time-supported $C^1$ curve $\phi:[0,\infty)\to V$,
$$
\int_0^\infty\!\bigl[(u,\partial_t\phi)_{L^2}+(u\otimes u,\nabla\phi)_{L^2}-\nu(\nabla u,\nabla\phi)_{L^2}\bigr]dt+(u_0,\phi(0))_{L^2}=0.
$$
It satisfies the initial energy inequality
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_0^t\|\nabla u(s)\|_2^2ds\le\|u_0\|_2^2\qquad(t\ge0),
$$
and a full-measure set $S\subset(0,\infty)$ such that for every $s\in S\cup\{0\}$ and $t\ge s$,
$$
\|u(t)\|_2^2+2\nu\int_s^t\|\nabla u(\tau)\|_2^2d\tau\le\|u(s)\|_2^2.
$$
Here spatial norms and pairings use unnormalized Lebesgue measure, $(u\otimes u):\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}u_i u_j\partial_j\phi_i$, and $\nabla u:\nabla\phi=\sum_{i,j}\partial_j u_i\partial_j\phi_i$. Thus the SI kinetic energy $E(t)=\frac{\rho_0}{2}\int_\Omega|u(t,x)|^2dx$ obeys
$$
E(t)+\mu\int_0^t\int_\Omega|\nabla u(s,x)|^2dx\,ds\le E(0).
$$
The no-slip condition is only the stated $H_0^1$ closure condition; the result supplies no pressure or pointwise wall trace.

The periodic mechanical model has a velocity field and a kinetic-energy inequality with viscous dissipation, but it has no temperature variable. The separate thermal model uses a positive temperature field $T$ in kelvin, a thermal energy density $e_{\mathrm{th}}(T)$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and heat flux $j_Q$ in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$; its adopted local balance is $\partial_t e_{\mathrm{th}}(T)+\operatorname{div}j_Q=0$ with insulated faces $j_Q\cdot n=0$. Its Fourier constitutive assumption is $j_Q=-K(x,T)\nabla T$, where the symmetric part of $K$ is positive semidefinite. The separate entropy-production theorem and constant-conductivity Neumann heat-evolution theorem retain their own regularity and initial-data conditions.

Neither branch identifies any part of the mechanical viscous dissipation with a source in the thermal balance, and the two branches use different domains. A coupled temperature evolution therefore requires an additional model assumption specifying the conversion of mechanical energy into heat and a common domain/field interface; it does not follow from the weak periodic continuation or from the thermal entropy and heat-evolution results.
